chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Anbasa al-Abid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Beware of disputes, for they occupy the heart, cause hypocrisy, and earn grudges.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and social consequences of engaging in disputes according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies quarreling (khushumah) not merely as a social friction but as a spiritual disease that clouds the heart and breeds hypocrisy (nifaq). This warning aligns with the Shia emphasis on purifying the inner self (tazkiyah), suggesting that persistent disputing erodes sincerity and cultivates lasting animosity (daga'in) among believers.
